subject: Biology
title: Life Processes: Chapter Introduction
summary: Even at rest your body keeps working: repair and maintenance need energy all the time. The four life processes: nutrition, respiration, transportation and excretion.
keyPoints: Even when we rest, **maintenance** (repair, upkeep) goes on, so the body needs **energy** all the time.
**Nutrition:** taking in food. Green plants make it (photosynthesis: autotrophs); we take it in (heterotrophs).
**Respiration:** breaking down food to release energy, mostly with oxygen, in the **mitochondria**.
**Transportation** carries food, oxygen and wastes (blood pumped by the heart); **excretion** removes harmful wastes (kidneys).

head: Process

rows: Takes in food (source of energy and materials)
Glucose + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O + energy (in mitochondria)

list: Autotrophs make their own food from simple substances (green plants, by photosynthesis).
Heterotrophs depend on food made by others (animals, fungi, most bacteria).
